purpose: reproduce the historical LCD CS-hold failure while changing only write-side CS framing and holding the readback observer constant

historical_failure.write_framing: CASET command, CASET data, RASET command, RASET data, RAMWR command, and pixel payload use separate CS-low intervals
historical_failure.readback_observer: SIO bitbang at approximately 500 kHz with one-microsecond delays and MISO sampling after each falling edge
historical_failure.observed_result: five solid fills pass; the four-colour pattern reads red/red/red/red with three mismatches

v1_inconclusive_attempt.observed_result: black and white solid fills pass; red, green, and blue solid fills fail; the pattern returns 0x7c00 for all samples with four mismatches

current_correct_driver.write_framing: CASET, RASET, RAMWR, and all pixel payload remain in one CS-low interval

promoted_backend.known_model_property: LCD command state survives CS rising and is covered by command_state_survives_cs_pulsing_between_bytes

cause_analysis.confirmed_major_confounder: v1 reproduced the historical write-side CS boundaries but retained a different RAMRD observer, so it was not the complete measurement setup that produced the frozen historical oracle
cause_analysis.causal_status: the observer difference is confirmed, but it cannot be declared the sole cause of the oracle mismatch until the controlled v2 experiment is measured
cause_analysis.unconfirmed_inference: the v1 raw values are exactly the values produced by a one-bit right rotation of the RGB666 18-bit stream; this is consistent with a read sampling or phase difference, but the electrical mechanism has not been measured and must not be treated as confirmed
cause_analysis.backend_risk_hypothesis: because the promoted LCD model preserves command state across CS pulses, it may accept the historical faulty write framing; this is a prediction, not an emulator result

controlled_experiment.independent_variable: write-side CS framing for CASET, RASET, RAMWR, and pixel payload
controlled_experiment.controlled_observer: the exact historical SIO bitbang RAMRD procedure in both baseline and fault builds

baseline.required_result: all five solid fills and the four-colour pattern pass on emulator and hardware

forbidden_changes: readback transport, clock, edge, delay, dummy-byte count, or colour conversion
test coordinates, expected colours, sample count, or mismatch calculation
backend source or LCD model before the first fault run

fixed.required_result: all five solid fills and the four-colour pattern pass on emulator and hardware

rejected_alternative.proposal: repeat the first source pixel in write_pixels_rgb565 so the four-colour pattern becomes red/red/red/red while solid fills remain unchanged
rejected_alternative.reason: this would create the old visible oracle by changing pixel progression, not reproduce the historical CS-hold defect or test the backend CS model; it is a different negative-conformance candidate

execution_order: implement and freeze the v2 baseline with the correct writer and historical observer
prove clean-clone reproducibility of the baseline BIN and UF2
run the baseline BIN in the emulator and the same-build UF2 through uf2loader on hardware; both must pass
derive the v2 fault commit by changing only write-side CS framing and freeze source, toolchain, BIN, UF2, bundle, and oracle evidence
run the fault UF2 through uf2loader on hardware
only if hardware matches the frozen fault oracle exactly, run the same-build fault BIN once in the frozen promoted backend and preserve the first result
compare reasons and classify the case
restore only the writer and prove the fixed BIN and UF2 pass on emulator and hardware

hardware_path.reason: the candidate exercises the normal PicoCalc application path and has no flash-layout or loader-reservation requirement

stop_conditions: baseline emulator or hardware result is not an exact PASS
clean-clone BIN or UF2 reproducibility fails
the fault diff changes the controlled observer or anything outside the change budget
hardware fault result differs from the frozen oracle
artifact or boot identity is incomplete
